featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Crossroad in Vile Parle and had one of the best dining experiences in Mumbai. The variety of food we ordered was impressive: Masala Papad, Butter Garlic Naan, Laccha Paratha, Paneer Chilly Dry, Paneer Tikka, Khichiya Papad, Lababdar Paneer, and Paneer Kadhai.

The Paneer Tikka, in particular, was a standout—it’s easily the best I’ve ever had. The food was fresh, flavorful, and served at just the right temperature. The restaurant maintains excellent hygiene, and the staff was not only open and friendly but also highly attentive to our preferences. We were pleasantly surprised with a complimentary snack while waiting for our food, a gesture that added to the overall experience.

One thing that sets Crossroad apart is the separate veg and non-veg kitchens, ensuring that everyone’s dietary preferences are respected. The quality of service here rivals that of many fine dining establishments in Mumbai, but at far more reasonable rates.

I highly recommend Crossroad to anyone looking for great food, drinks, and top-notch service in Mumbai. It’s definitely a place worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Mashelkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Utasv is a simple and elegant restaurant for family and friends. This is a Veg restaurant. Just because it’s a veg restaurant they have introduce a lot of innovative dishes to the menu and all. This restaurant is small and cozy with around 7-8 tables with a total sitting capacity of 40 people. This is an old restaurant who has kept them self-updated with latest food trends and drinks. The Ambiance of the restaurant is also smile and plan with nothing much in designs.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. I would recommend you to try this dish and pair it with a sweet mocktail.

The second dish was The Corn Cheese Kurkure. This is a very good veg starters and I would go for this dish over many non-veg starters. This is a crispy dish with a very creamy filling. The inner filling is made up of palak paste mixed with cheese and corn, which is wrapped around spring roll wrap and the entire thing is deep fried until golden brown. This dish is served in shot glasses filled in green chutney and garnished with cheese. You can eat this dish like a finger sticks and its really enjoyable dish.

The Next dish was the Falafal Pocket. This is a middle eastern dish which is prepared very nicely by the restaurant. Basically what this dish is a fluffy form of pita bread which is stuffed with a creamy salad. This restaurant fills the bread with very little salad and serves the rest as side dish so as to fill it more as per your individual needs. They also serve Humus sauce which is prepared by their chef to go along with this dish. The texture of the dish is very tempting wanting you to fill it with more of the salad. If you want something new to eat go for this dish.

Then I went for the Main course in which the first was Panner in Coriander Sauce. This was a nice pan Asian dish prepared with delicate sauce. The Texture of the dish was dark and thick whereas the aroma was very light on the nose. This is a stirred fried dish which is cooked along with spring onion , scallops and herbs. The panner is soft and tender and well submersed in the flavor of the Coriander sauce. A must try dish along with some drink.

Next up was the Dunger Panner Biriyani. This dish was more on presentation then its taste. The texture of the dish was rich and the aroma was very strong everyone in the hotel could smell the dish as it comes to your table.  The dish is mixed with a creamy panners and aromatic rice. This dish is best suited to have it along with a group of people at the end.

The last dish was the Desert i.e. Gulab Jamun Cheese Cake. The cake is exactly as it sounds it to be. This is a cheese cake filled with Gulab Jamun throughout. The cake is light with a crummy base and filled with lots of Gulab Jamun. I really liked this dish and ended up eating 2 of it. I recommend you to try this dish for sure

The variety they offer is fantastic, and the quality is consistently top-notch. Despite the 1+1 seating setup, the place is always crowded, which speaks volumes about how popular it is. If you're a fan of South Indian-style seafood, you're in for a treat—their preparations really stand out.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

They have both AC (higher prices) and non-AC sections. Waiting time for AC usually is 15 minutes or more, unless you reach early by 12.15 or 12.30 pm for lunch. We chose the non-AC with good overhead fans, since we were hungry and it was nearly 2 pm.

Each item was served hot, with the regular accompaniments, onion, lime, specially requested pickle, hot sambhar and coconut chutney.
They serve cold Distilled water in Stainless steel glasses, which bypasses the need for any bottled mineral water.
Good quality tissues and an easily accessible washbasin make it convenient for clean up after a finger licking, palate tickling vegetarian meal. Being 100% vegetarian is the added advantage here. They accept all kinds of payments with no extra surcharge or service charges. The regulatory 5% GST is added to your bill amount.
A good hearty meal for five cost us less than 1500 including tips.
Even if you are very hungry and are good eaters, surely you won't spend more than 400-450 per person at this absolutely genuine vegetarian restaurant catering mostly to the College and school kids, especially during day time and the locals living in Andheri West, especially in the evenings.
Valet parking is available.

We recently dined at Govinda’s Bistro, located inside the serene ISKCON Juhu Temple, and the experience was truly delightful from start to finish. The calm, spiritual ambiance of the temple sets the perfect tone for a soulful meal, making it much more than just a restaurant visit.

The lotus stem dish was beautifully cooked perfectly tender with a satisfying crunch, well-seasoned, and full of earthy flavors. The pizza was another highlight, with a crisp base, generous toppings, and a rich, cheesy flavor that didn’t feel heavy. The pasta was creamy and indulgent, yet light on the palate, showing excellent balance in seasoning and texture. The Thai curry with basil rice was absolutely delicious—the curry was fragrant, mildly spiced, and creamy, pairing perfectly with the aromatic basil rice.

To end the meal on a sweet note, we had the gulkand ice cream, which was refreshing, unique, and incredibly soothing. Its delicate rose flavors made it the perfect dessert to round off such a satisfying meal.

Overall, Govinda’s Bistro delivers exceptional taste, variety, and quality, proving that food made without onion and garlic can still be rich, flavorful, and memorable. featured_reviews.name: Amey M
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a Satvic restaurant that serves food on a thali as well as à la carte basis. All items are onion- and garlic-free, yet the taste competes well with many non-Satvic restaurants. The ambience is pleasant, noise-free, and parking is available on a pay-and-park basis. Their menu changes daily, which is a nice touch.

They offer 2 salads, 4 starters, 4 vegetables, 3 types of rice, pasta, 2 dals, 4 flavours of welcome drinks, 3 sweets, and 2 desserts. The quality and quantity are good.

However, consistency in taste is an issue. Don’t expect the same flavour every day—especially the dal tadka, which often tastes like simple plain dal. Since the food is served buffet-style, you may not get the full dining experience you expect.

It seems they use soda in many items, and some dishes share the same gravy—for example, pasta and a couple of vegetables having a similar base. They also serve more liquid items, possibly to control quantity. Serving multiple items on small plates can also reduce the overall satisfaction.

Overall, the variety is impressive, the ambience is good, and the food is decent—but consistency and preparation style could be improved.

featured_reviews.name: Mitesh Goyani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan was packed as always — we just made it in time to grab a table.

The must-haves here are the Tatte Idli, which is absolutely lip-smacking, and their strong filter coffee with minimal sugar. We also loved the Mysore Sada, Tomato Capsicum Uttapam, and the Rasam Wada.
The chutneys are consistently excellent and truly elevate the meal.

Unfortunately, we couldn’t try the stew this time as they had run out of it.

However, we’re not particularly big fans of their sambar.

Overall, still a great spot for a satisfying South Indian meal.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful breakfast experience at Dakshinayan. The restaurant is very spacious and comfortable, making it a great place to enjoy a relaxed family outing. I have visited this place multiple times, and the food quality and service have always been consistently good.

We tried Mini Masala Idli, Steamed Idli, Medu Vada, Masala Medu Vada, Coconut Sevai, Raagi Masala Dosa, Adai Masala Dosa, Rava Masala Dosa, Bisi Bele Bhat, and Filter Coffee. Everything was delicious and freshly prepared. The Raagi Masala Dosa and Filter Coffee are definitely a must-try here.

The service is quick and courteous, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience. We had a fantastic Sunday morning breakfast with family. It’s advisable to visit early in the morning if you prefer a less crowded atmosphere.

Highly recommended for authentic South Indian breakfast lovers!

featured_reviews.name: Amit Mehra
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were a party of 3 for lunch on a Wednesday . Getting a table was easy as we were there around 12.00 noon. Around 12.30pm the restaurant was practically full.
The seating is spread out , the space is nice and bright and very clean . The aircon facing us was on high cool so we had them turn it down and they obliged .
The food was amazing - for drinks we had the fresh sugar cane juice ,filter coffee and fresh lime soda , all of which were really good - the coffee could have been hotter .
Starters we had rasam vada & kancheepuram idli to share - both were well made - vada was soft and so was the idli. The rasam was top notch.
Mains we shared a ghee masala dosa , masala vada and pesarattu -all three were really good .
Desserts we had were falooda kulfi, kesar pista kulfi and filter coffee affogato. All three did not disappoint.
Service would have been 5* except for a very reluctant server who stood across the table staring at everything but did not take orders or help.
The restaurant sells two kinds of podi and rasam/ sambar powder in their own brand .
